skill.name: security-fundamentals
skill.description: Guides reviews of authentication, authorization, input handling, data exposure, and other OWASP Top 10 risks.
skill.summary: Security review checklist for user-facing code and common web application risks.
skill.author: DanielPodolsky

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples in a defensive security checklist. The skill warns against unsafe patterns such as eval, innerHTML, weak password hashing, and SQL string interpolation; no executable code, prompt injection attempt, data exfiltration intent, or command execution behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static security scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep unsafe examples clearly marked with warning labels and safe alternatives so reviewers understand they are educational anti-patterns.

content.value_statement: Security mistakes often appear in common areas like authentication, authorization, input handling, and data exposure. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused checklist for finding those risks during review.
actual_capabilities: Applies a security checklist to authentication, authorization, input handling, database queries, file uploads, APIs, and response data.
Highlights OWASP Top 10 risks with unsafe and safer examples.
Prompts reviewers to ask ownership, trust, exposure, secrets, and injection questions.
Lists red flags such as dynamic code execution, innerHTML with user data, missing rate limits, broad CORS, and weak password hashing.
Provides a pre-deploy checklist covering validation, HTTPS, CSRF, rate limiting, sensitive data, authorization, and security headers.
limitations: It is a review guide, not an automated vulnerability scanner.
It does not run tests, inspect dependencies, or verify runtime configuration by itself.
It focuses on common web application risks and may not cover specialized threat models.
It depends on the reviewer to apply the checklist to the relevant code paths.

use_cases.title: Review a new API endpoint
use_cases.description: Check input validation, authorization, sensitive response fields, rate limiting, and security headers before merge.

use_cases.title: Mentor junior engineers
use_cases.description: Use Socratic questions to guide engineers toward secure reasoning without simply giving answers.

use_cases.title: Prepare for production deployment
use_cases.description: Run through the deploy checklist to confirm secrets, HTTPS, CSRF, injection defenses, and access controls are addressed.

prompt_templates.title: Check this endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one route or handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security fundamentals checklist to review this endpoint. Focus on input validation, authorization, and sensitive data exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Review authentication changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of login or session logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authentication changes for password handling, token expiry, secure transmission, logging, and brute-force protections.

prompt_templates.title: Audit access control paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across multiple protected resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the security fundamentals skill to these protected routes. Identify missing ownership checks, role checks, and server-side authorization gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a security pre-deploy review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a pre-deploy security review using this checklist. Group findings by injection, XSS, CSRF, data exposure, authentication, authorization, and misconfiguration.

output_examples.input: Review a user profile endpoint before merge.
output: Flags missing ownership checks on profile access.
Recommends returning only necessary user fields.
Asks whether sensitive fields can appear in logs or URLs.
Checks password hashing and token expiry.
Looks for rate limiting on authentication attempts.
Verifies that detailed errors are not exposed in production.
Confirms server-side validation and parameterized queries.
Checks HTTPS, CSRF protection, and security headers.
Reviews CORS settings and sensitive response data.

best_practices: Use the checklist before merging changes that handle users, credentials, files, or API data.
Ask ownership and trust questions for every protected resource.
Pair each unsafe pattern with a safer implementation recommendation.
anti_patterns: Treating the checklist as proof that code is secure without reviewing the actual implementation.
Relying on client-side validation or client-side authorization as the main defense.
Ignoring logs, URLs, and error messages when checking for sensitive data exposure.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically scan code for vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured review checklist and questions for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to apply during review.

faq.question: Which security topics does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes input validation, authentication, authorization, data exposure, injection, XSS, CSRF, rate limiting, CORS, and security headers.

faq.question: Can it replace a full penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports secure code review, but it does not replace threat modeling, dynamic testing, dependency review, or a penetration test.

faq.question: Is it useful for mentoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Socratic questions that help junior engineers reason about trust, ownership, exposure, secrets, and injection.

faq.question: Can it be used before deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a pre-deploy checklist for secrets, HTTPS, validation, injection defenses, XSS, CSRF, rate limits, data exposure, authorization, and headers.

faq.question: Does it include dangerous executable code?
faq.answer: No. The unsafe patterns are Markdown examples that teach reviewers what to avoid.
